title: Invoice Access Hunt
subtitle: Find and fix an IDOR in Lumen Health's billing API
summary: Lumen Health's billing API authenticates callers but never checks which patient an invoice belongs to. Read a record you should not see, then close the gap through the authenticated admin API.
scenario: You are reviewing a patient billing portal for Lumen Health. The API is protected by a login, but the security team suspects object-level authorization was never implemented. Find an invoice belonging to another patient, capture the evidence marker, then remediate the endpoint and prove it with a live check.
learningObjectives: Recognise broken object level authorization (IDOR) in a real API
Use an authenticated session to enumerate object identifiers
Apply and verify an ownership check through a deployment API
Explain why authentication alone is not authorization
authorizedScope: Only the Lumen Health training portal inside this session. All patients, invoices and payments are fictional.
riskSummary: An IDOR in billing exposes protected health and payment records across tenants. Attackers enumerate sequential identifiers and exfiltrate records without ever breaking authentication.
remediation: Enforce object ownership on every record fetch, return 403 (not 404 with data) for foreign objects, and log authorization denials with the caller and object id.
conclusion: You demonstrated a cross-tenant data exposure using nothing but an authenticated session, then remediated it by turning on enforced ownership in the portal policy and proving the denial with a live validator.

objectives.title: Read another patient's invoice
objectives.description: Sign in with the demo account, inspect your own invoice API responses, then request a neighbouring invoice identifier that belongs to a different patient. The memo of that invoice contains the flag.
objectives.evidencePrompt: Submit the flag from the foreign invoice memo.

hints.text: Log in with curl and keep the cookie: `curl -si -c cookies.txt -d 'email=analyst%40lumenhealth.example&password=lumen2024' $CF_TARGET_URL/login`.
Your invoices are INV-1041 and INV-1042. The API responds at /api/invoices/<id>; try ids around the range you see.

objectives.title: Enforce ownership on the invoice API
objectives.description: Use the authenticated admin API to enable ownership checks, then run the live check. It signs in as the demo patient and confirms a foreign invoice is rejected while their own invoice still loads.
objectives.evidencePrompt: Run the live check after changing the policy.

hints.text: Read the current policy with `labctl policy get`, then apply `{"enforceOwnership": true}` with `labctl policy apply`.

walkthrough.title: Sign in and keep the session
walkthrough.body: The portal sets an HttpOnly cookie. Save it with curl so the API trusts you.

walkthrough.title: Enumerate the invoice API
walkthrough.body: Your list shows the identifiers you own. Request a neighbouring identifier and read the JSON memo.
walkthrough.snippet: for id in 1098 1099 1100; do curl -s -b cookies.txt "$CF_TARGET_URL/api/invoices/INV-$id"; echo; done

walkthrough.title: Apply the ownership policy
walkthrough.body: The admin API accepts a single switch. Applying it makes the API compare the invoice owner to your session.

walkthrough.title: Verify the fix
walkthrough.body: Re-request the foreign invoice: it must now return 403, while your own invoice still returns 200. Then run the objective's live check.
